Title: Info
Text:
Now, you have the possibility to describe your forms textually, and to save them in a 4D object or a file.

Then at runtime, you can load your forms from a 4D object or a file that contains the description of the form.

The following commands have been updated to support 4D objects or path name:

* Open form window
* DIALOG
* FORM SET INPUT
* FORM SET OUTPUT
* OBJECT SET SUBFORM
* OBJECT GET SUBFORM
* FORM LOAD
* Print form
* Current form name

Title: Hello World
Text:
★ Here a simple example with a static text and a button in the page 1.

★ On the left, you have the textual description of form.

★ On the right, click on the "Load button" to load with the OBJECT SET SUBFORM command the result in a subform.
DescriptionForm:
{
"name": "HelloWorld",

... list of form parameters ...

"pages": [ ... list of pages ...

 null, ... page 0 ...

{ ... page 1 ...

"objects": { ... list of form objects in page 1 ...

 "text": {
"type": "text",
"text": "Hello world !",
"left": 20, "top": 20, "width": 200, "height": 20
},

"button": {
"type": "button",
"text": "OK",
"left": 120, "top": 40, "width": 100, "height": 20
}
}
}
]
}

Title: Confirm dialog
Text:
★ Here an example with a confirm dialog.

★ On the right, enter your question and your additional message, then click on the button to display the confirm dialog with the DIALOG command.
DescriptionForm:
{
"name": "confirmDialog",
"windowTitle": "Warning",
"windowMinWidth": 400,
"windowMinHeight": 200,
"pages": [
null,
{
"objects": {
"title": {
"type": "text",
"text": "Define the title text",
"left": 80, "top": 20, "width": 300, "height": 40,
"fontTheme": "main",
"sizingX": "grow", "sizingY": "fixed"
},
"subTitle": {
"type": "text",
"text": "Define the subTitle text",
"left": 80, "top": 70, "width": 300,"height": 60,
"fontTheme": "additional",
"sizingX": "grow", "sizingY": "fixed"
},
"warningIcon": {
"type": "picture",
"left": 20, "top": 20, "width": 40, "height": 40,
"pictureFormat": "scaled",
"picture": "/RESOURCES/Images/Alert.png"
},
"btnOK": {
"type": "button",
"text": "OK",
"action": "Accept",
"left": 280, "top": 160, "width": 100, "height": 20,
"defaultButton": true,
"sizingX": "move", "sizingY": "move"
},
"btnCancel": {
"type": "button",
"text": "Cancel",
"action": "Cancel",
"left": 160, "top": 160, "width": 100, "height": 20,
"sizingX": "move", "sizingY": "move"
}
}
}
]
}

Title: Table form
Text:
★ Here is an example with a output form and a input form for the "Person" table.

★ Click on the "Open dialog" button to open the output form.

★ The command DIALOG opens the output form. The FORM SET INPUT command is used to define the input form. To reminder, the "editSubrecord" and "addSubrecord" standard actions use a input table form.
